production.note: US model years. BMW NA's M5 history lists the car as '2000 – 2003 E39 M5'; BMW NA's first press kit is 'Press Kit MY 2000' (bmw-us-2000-m5-specs).

displacementL.note: 4,941 cc ('Displacement, cu in./cc 4941/302' as printed). BMW marketed it as a 5-liter engine; the rounded cc figure is used.

transmission.note: 'Manual transmission Getrag Type D, 6-speed'; no other transmission is listed.

powerHp.note: BMW NA's rating from its 2002 sheet. Quote: "Power @ rpm, hp SAE net 394 @ 6600". BMW NA's 2019 history gives the same "394 hp @ 6,600 rpm" (bmw-us-2019-m5-edition-35). BMW NA's 2000 sheet printed "Power @ rpm, hp SAE net 400 @ 6600" (bmw-us-2000-m5-specs) for the same 4,941 cc engine; 400 is numerically the European PS figure. See discrepancies.

weightLb.note: Sedan with the 6-speed manual (the only configuration), from BMW NA's 2002 sheet (curb weight 4,023 lb). The 2000 sheet reads "Curb weight, lb. 4024" (bmw-us-2000-m5-specs), and BMW NA's 2019 history repeats 4,024 lb (bmw-us-2019-m5-edition-35).

discrepancies.reason: BMW NA's 2000 sheet rates the engine 400 hp SAE net at 6,600 rpm; its 2002 sheet and its 2019 history rate the same 4,941 cc engine 394 hp at 6,600 rpm. 400 is numerically the European PS rating, so the later figure is a restatement, not a mechanical change. The 2001 and 2003 sheets were not found.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 394 hp with reference model year 2002: it is the figure on BMW NA's later period sheet and the one BMW NA itself uses today for this car.

discrepancies.reason: Model year: BMW NA's 2000 and 2002 sheets differ by one pound.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 4,023 lb to match the 2002 reference year.
